title: Orientation Week for incoming international students
text:
Orientation Week for incoming international students

The Orientation Week is run by the VŠE International Office one week before the start of the academic year to introduce new international students to the campus, study system, the city of Prague and Czech culture.

Typical components:
1. ESN VŠE Prague activities (cultural, social).
2. Study-programme-specific sessions run by programme coordinators.
3. International Office programme (past example: Library lecture, Intercultural Competences, Cultural History of Czech Lands, Culture Shock lecture, Czech Language Guide, Chill-Out Zone, Team Game).

The detailed calendar for the next intake is published on the Admission Office site – check the page above a few weeks before arrival.

# Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – general information

title: Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – general information
text:
Visa and residence permit for study in the Czech Republic – general information

## General information only – verify with the official authorities
Non-EU/EEA students typically need either:
- **Long-stay visa for study (90+ days)**, applied at a Czech embassy/consulate before arrival.
- **Long-stay residence permit for study**, applied at the Czech embassy/consulate (renewable in Czechia).

The decision depends on the length and type of study. As of 2026-10-25 the live URL https://www.mvcr.cz/mvcren/article/long-stay-visa.aspx could not be verified live in this run – marked as a gap below.

EU/EEA/Swiss students do not need a visa but must register with the Foreign Police if staying >30 days and register for health insurance.

Action: always consult the **VŠE International Office** and the **Czech Ministry of the Interior (mvcr.cz)** for your personal case. Do not rely on third-party summaries.

title: Czech embassies and consulates abroad (MZV / Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
text:
Czech embassies and consulates abroad (MZV / Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

For visa applications, contact the Czech embassy or consulate in your home country. The MZV portal lists all diplomatic missions, current public holidays and consular fees.

The live URL https://www.mzv.cz/inp/en/index.html could not be retrieved on 2026-10-25 in this run – listed as gap. Confirm the link on the MZV website before sending a student to it.

title: Health insurance and medical care
text:
Health insurance and medical care

International students must have valid health insurance covering their stay in the Czech Republic. Two main categories:
- **EU/EEA/Swiss students**: use the EHIC (European Health Insurance Card) from home plus supplementary commercial insurance recommended.
- **Non-EU students**: a contract with a Czech-approved insurance company (e.g. PVZP, Slavia, Maxima) is normally a requirement of the long-stay visa/residence permit.

General practitioner (praktický lékař) and hospitals are accessible with valid insurance. Emergency: **155** (ambulance) or **112** (single European emergency number).

title: VŠE dormitories and student housing
text:
VŠE dormitories and student housing

VŠE student dormitories are managed by the Správa kolejí a menzy (SKM). The SKM English portal https://skm.vse.cz/english/ is the canonical place for housing applications, pricing and rules.

> Gap: live retrieval of https://skm.vse.cz/english/ and https://skm.vse.cz/english/dormitories/ failed during this run (network error). Treat the application deadlines, prices and room types as **unverified**. Direct students to SKM by email/phone from the live site before they commit to a housing plan.

title: Private accommodation in Prague – general guidance
text:
Private accommodation in Prague – general guidance

VŠE maintains an Accommodation Centre page under Campus Services. Common private options in Prague:
- Shared flats (flat-shares) on bezrealitky.cz, sreality.cz, expats.cz.
- Student residences run by private operators.
- Facebook groups "Flat in Prague / Pronájem Praha".

Always sign a written contract, never transfer deposits before viewing, and check that the landlord is registered for VAT if charging short-term fees.

# InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 1. Login, English language switch and password reset
- **Portal URL:** https://insis.vse.cz/ (or via the official mobile app *My College* on iOS/Android).
- **Username format:** Typically 4 letters + 2 numbers based on your surname and name (e.g. `novj01`).
- **Switch to English:** Click the **British flag icon / EN** in the top-right corner of any InSIS page.
- **Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA):** Required for all logins using an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator or Google Authenticator) on your mobile phone.
- **Forgotten password:** If you cannot log in, use the password reset link on the initial admissions application portal, or visit the IT Helpdesk in person with your student ID / passport (Žižkov Old Building SB or New Building NB).

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 2. Personal data, Prague address and Czech bank account
- **Where to add Czech bank account:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Bank Accounts (Bankovní účty)**. Mandatory for receiving accommodation scholarships, merit scholarships, and study fee refunds.
- **Update Prague address and phone:** InSIS → **Personal Management (Osobní management)** → **Personal Data (Osobní údaje)**. You must keep your current Czech residence address and emergency contact phone number updated for official university notifications.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 3. Weekly timetable and Google/Apple Calendar export
- **View timetable:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **My Timetable (Rozvrh)**. Displays weekly class schedules, lecture halls, and seminar rooms.
- **Campus room code decoder:** `RB` = Rajská budova, `SB` = Stará budova, `NB` = Nová budova, `JM` = Jižní Město. The first digit is the floor number (e.g. `RB 101` is Rajská 1st floor, `NB 403` is Nová 4th floor).
- **Sync with calendar:** Click **Export to iCal / ICS feed link** in the timetable toolbar to sync your VŠE class schedule automatically with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 4. Coursework submission (Odevzdávárna / Drop-in box)
- **Where to submit assignments:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Student's Coursework Submission (Odevzdávárna / Drop-in box)**.
- Select your course and assignment topic, then upload homework, presentation slides, or project files before the deadline.
- Always check that the file uploaded completely and that the submission timestamp is recorded before the deadline expires.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 5. Continuous evaluation, test points and grades (Sheet of results)
- **Check points and grades:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **My Lectures / Sheet of Results (Záznamník učitele / Průběžné hodnocení)**.
- Displays continuous test scores, seminar attendance points, midterms, and final exam grades recorded by your professors.
- **Grading scale at VŠE:**
  - 1 = Excellent (*Výborně*, 90–100%)
  - 2 = Very Good (*Velmi dobře*, 75–89%)
  - 3 = Good (*Dobře*, 60–74%)
  - 4+ / 4 = Failed (*Nevyhověl*, under 60%)
  - Zápočet (z) = Satisfied / ungraded course requirement.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 6. Exam registration, dates and cancellation (Přihlašování na zkoušky)
- **Register for exams:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Exam Dates and Registration (Přihlašování na zkoušky)**.
- Browse available examination dates (*řádné termíny*), check room locations, examiner names, and capacity limits.
- **Deregistration / Cancellation:** If you cannot attend an exam, you must cancel your registration in InSIS before the cancellation deadline (typically 24 hours prior). Unexcused absences count as a failed attempt (grade 4) and deduct from your retake attempts.
- **Exam retakes (Opravný termín):** If you fail an exam, you are entitled to up to 2 retake dates within the semester exam period.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 7. Official Electronic Confirmation of Study (Potvrzení o studiu)
- **Generate digitally signed PDF:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Student Confirmation** → click **Electronic Confirmation of Study**.
- The PDF is generated with an official Qualified Electronic Stamp (digitally sealed) accepted by the Czech Foreign Police, OAMP MVČR, transit authorities (PID / Lítačka), banks, and embassies.
- The signed PDF appears ready for download in **Student's Portal** → **Document Storage (Úschovna dokumentů)** within approx. 30–60 minutes.
- **Certified paper copy:** If a physical paper stamp is required, bring the digital PDF on a flash drive to any CzechPOINT post office for official authorized conversion (*konverze dokumentů*).

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 8. Study financing, Variable Symbol (VS) and fee payments
- **Check tuition and payment details:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Study Financing (Financování studia)**.
- Find your unique, personalized **Variable Symbol (VS)** needed to pair bank payments.
- Access the online payment gateway to pay tuition or fee balances directly by debit/credit card, or scan the Czech QR code with your mobile banking app.
- Check payment history and verify whether your payment has been marked as received by the bursar.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 9. Accommodation scholarship application (Ubytovací stipendium)
- **Where to apply:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **My Studies** → **Scholarships (Žádost o ubytovací stipendium)**.
- Available to full-time students whose permanent residence is outside Prague.
- Must be submitted online twice a year (autumn and spring windows).
- Payout is processed quarterly directly into the Czech bank account specified in InSIS.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 10. Study plan audit, completed credits and credit vouchers
- **Audit degree progress:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Check of Study Plan (Kontrola studijního plánu)**.
- Displays completed ECTS credits vs required credits across mandatory (`sP`), optional (`sV`), and faculty groups, as well as your cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA / *studijní průměr*).
- Check your remaining **credit voucher balance** (Bachelor students start with 216 vouchers; Master students start with 144 vouchers).

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 11. Official electronic requests via Document Office (Úřadovna)
- **Where to submit official requests:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Document Office (Úřadovna)** → **Submit a new application**.
- Used for official administrative petitions to the Dean or Vice-Dean, including:
  - Official apology for illness/absence from study or exams (with medical certificate).
  - Recognition of previous university credits or Erasmus study courses.
  - Request for individual study plan.
  - Request for interruption of studies.
  - Correction of course registration or credit voucher discrepancies.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 12. Final thesis, plagiarism check and state final exams (Státnice)
- **Thesis topic and supervisor:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Thesis Topics (Témata závěrečných prací)**. Propose or register your thesis topic and supervisor (*vedoucí práce*).
- **Electronic thesis submission:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **Final Thesis Submission (Odevzdání závěrečné práce)**. Upload the final PDF text of your Bachelor's or Master's thesis and abstract before the semester deadline.
- InSIS automatically routes your thesis to **Theses.cz** for plagiarism analysis.
- **State Final Exams:** InSIS → **Student's Portal** → **State Final Exams (SZZ / Státnice)** to register for defense and state exam dates.

title: InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide
text:
InSIS – complete student portal navigation and services guide

## 13. Course and teacher evaluation survey (Studentská evaluace)
- At the end of each semester, InSIS opens the anonymous **Student Evaluation of Teaching**.
- Access via **Student's Portal** → **Student Evaluation (Evaluace)** to provide anonymous feedback on course content, professors, seminar tutors, and materials.

title: Employment during studies – general information
text:
Employment during studies – general information

## General information only – verify with the authorities
- **EU/EEA/Swiss students**: free access to the Czech labour market; no work permit required.
- **Non-EU students holding a long-stay visa or residence permit for study**: employment is generally allowed without a separate work permit, but conditions (max hours during studies, mandatory employer notification of the employment office) apply and change frequently.

Critical: confirm the current rules on the Czech Ministry of the Interior website and with the **VŠE International Office** before signing any employment contract.

title: Cost of living and budgeting in Prague – general guidance
text:
Cost of living and budgeting in Prague – general guidance

Approximate monthly student budget (figures change – always cross-check on official sites):
- Dormitory bed: low-mid range shared, often the cheapest option (see SKM).
- Private flat share: ~8,000–14,000 CZK/month outside city centre (varies by district).
- Food: ~6,000–9,000 CZK/month (cheaper with university canteens + ISIC discount + Lítačka discounts).
- Transport: long-term student PID pass significantly cheaper than single tickets.
- Mobile + internet: combined bundles from ~600 CZK/month.

Save money by using ISIC, student Lítačka, daily lunch menus (polední menu / denní menu), and the Nesnězeno and LOKNI apps.

title: Czech language basics for international students
text:
Czech language basics for international students

VŠE programmes are taught in English; daily life is mostly in Czech. Practical tips:
- Learn the basics: *Dobrý den* (hello), *Prosím* (please), *Děkuji* (thanks), *Promiňte* (excuse me), *Kolik to stojí?* (How much is it?).
- Public transport announcements are bilingual on key stations.
- VŠE offers a Czech language lecture during Orientation Week and short courses through the University of the Third Age / language centres.

Czech films recommended by VŠE Ambassadors (Instagram, 2 days before save date): *Anthropoid*, *Waves (Vlny)*, *Kolya (Kolja)*.

title: Czech culture, history and student traditions
text:

Czech Republic sits in Central Europe with Germanic, Slavic and Habsburg influences. The Orientation Week "Cultural History of Czech Lands" lecture is the recommended primer.

Traditions to know: Christmas markets (Advent), Easter whip tradition (pomlázka), beer culture (Czech pubs are family-friendly at lunch), name days, anniversaries of 1989 Velvet Revolution on 17 November.

## How to pair payments: InSIS Variable Symbol (VS)
- Every student has a unique **Variable Symbol (VS)** generated automatically in the InSIS portal under **Student Portal → Study Financing (Financování studia)**.
- **Mandatory:** You must always include your exact Variable Symbol in the payment details. Without the Variable Symbol, the university accounting system cannot pair the payment with your student account.

- **Bank transfer charges:** Always select the **OUR** option (sender bears all bank transfer charges). If intermediary or receiving bank charges are deducted from the tuition amount, the payment is treated as incomplete.

# Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE

title: Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE
text:
Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE

## Internal VŠE assessment for admission (edu.vse.cz)
- Because VŠE holds institutional accreditation, it has the legal authority to assess foreign secondary and higher education directly for the admission procedure.
- General state nostrification is **not required** for most applicants if you use VŠE's internal assessment via the portal https://edu.vse.cz/.
- The internal assessment starts automatically after submitting and paying for your admission application in InSIS.
- The internal evaluation is valid exclusively for enrollment into study programmes at VŠE.

title: Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE
text:
Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE

## Required documents and legal verification
- **Bachelor applicants:** Officially certified copy of high school graduation certificate / secondary school leaving diploma + certified copy of transcript of grades / hours.
- **Master applicants:** Officially certified copy of Bachelor's degree diploma + diploma supplement or complete academic transcript.
- **Legal verification of documents:**
  - **Apostille:** Required for countries that are signatories to the Hague Apostille Convention (e.g. USA, India, UK, Turkey, Ukraine).
  - **Superlegalization:** Required for countries without the Hague Convention (verified by ministry of foreign affairs and the Czech embassy).
  - **Exemption:** Countries with bilateral legal assistance treaties with the Czech Republic (e.g. Slovakia, Poland, Hungary, Austria, Germany) do not need apostille or superlegalization.
- **Translations:** All documents issued in languages other than Czech, Slovak, or English must have an official certified translation into Czech or English attached.

title: Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE
text:
Foreign education assessment and nostrification at VŠE

## General state nostrification
- If a student needs recognition of their foreign degree for general legal purposes in the Czech Republic (outside VŠE admissions, e.g. for employment or public administration), they must submit a formal application for general recognition under the Higher Education Act to a Czech public university with a matching accredited programme.

# InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## VŠE credit voucher system
- VŠE uses a virtual credit voucher system to measure study progress and allow flexibility.
- Each incoming student receives a voucher pool:
  - **Bachelor's students:** 216 vouchers (180 for standard degree requirements + 36 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).
  - **Master's students:** 144 vouchers (120 for standard degree requirements + 24 reserve vouchers = 20% safety margin).
- **How vouchers work:** 1 ECTS credit = 1 voucher. When enrolling in a course, the corresponding vouchers are deducted. Passing the course converts those vouchers into earned ECTS credits. Failing an enrolled course consumes the vouchers permanently without earning credits.
- If a student runs out of vouchers and has fewer vouchers remaining than ECTS needed to graduate, studies are terminated.

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## Step-by-step how to enroll in a course in InSIS
1. **Sign in to InSIS:** Log in at https://insis.vse.cz/ with your VŠE username and password.
2. **Open Student's Portal:** In the main menu, navigate to **My Study** (or *My College*) → **Student's Portal**.
3. **Open Registration/Enrollment:** Click on **Registration/Enrollment** (Registrace/Zápisy).
4. **Browse Course Categories:** At the bottom of the page, click the course category indicator corresponding to your study plan:
   - `sP`: Compulsory courses (Povinné předměty)
   - `sV`: Elective/optional courses (Volitelné předměty)
   - Language groups or faculty-specific elective groups.
5. **Select and Add:** Check the boxes next to your desired courses and click **Add selected courses**.
6. **Select Timetable Slot (Mandatory):** In the **Timetable** column, click **Select** to pick your time slot. If a course has both a lecture and a seminar/exercise, you must choose time slots for both. The status icon turns green when complete.
7. **Verify Schedule:** Click **Display Timetables** to visually inspect your weekly calendar and ensure there are no overlapping classes.

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## Course registration and enrollment rounds
Registration in InSIS is split into clearly separated phases:
1. **Pre-registration (Orders):** Students express interest by ordering compulsory and elective courses. This phase is **not first-come, first-served**; submitting on day 1 or the final day gives equal priority.
2. **Automated processing:** InSIS allocates seats based on priority rules (curriculum requirements, earned credits, study plan group).
3. **Enrollment Round 1:** Management and confirmation of compulsory courses.
4. **Enrollment Round 2:** Enrollment of compulsory and pre-registered optional/elective courses.
5. **Enrollment Round 3 (Open changes):** Students can enroll in any open course across faculties that has remaining free capacity, even if not pre-registered.
6. **Add/Drop period:** Changes can still be made during the first week of teaching in the semester.

title: InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE
text:
InSIS course registration, rounds and credit voucher system at VŠE

## Minimum semester credits and exam retakes
- **First-semester threshold:** Students must earn at least **20 ECTS credits** in their first semester to remain eligible for subsequent semester enrollment. Standard full-time study load is 30 ECTS per semester (60 ECTS per academic year).
- **Exam retakes:** If a student fails an exam on the regular attempt, they are entitled to up to **two retake attempts** (opravný termín) within the examination period of the same semester.

title: Foreign police registration and residence permit extensions in Prague
text:
Foreign police registration and residence permit extensions in Prague

## Foreign Police registration duty upon arrival
- **Non-EU/EEA students:** Must report their arrival to the Foreign Police (*Cizinecká policie*) within **3 business days** of entering the Czech Republic if living in private accommodation. If staying in a VŠE university dormitory or licensed hotel, the accommodation provider reports the stay automatically.
- **EU/EEA/Swiss students:** Must register with the Foreign Police within **30 days** of arrival if their intended stay exceeds 30 days (unless registered by the dormitory).
- **Foreign Police Prague address:**
  - Department of Foreign Police (Oddělení pobytových agend): Olšanská 2176/2, 130 51 Praha 3 – Žižkov.
  - Documents to bring: valid passport, proof of accommodation (lease contract or owner declaration), proof of travel medical insurance.

title: Foreign police registration and residence permit extensions in Prague
text:
Foreign police registration and residence permit extensions in Prague

## Residence permit extension at OAMP MVČR
- The Department for Asylum and Migration Policy of the Ministry of the Interior (OAMP MVČR) handles long-term stays, long-stay residence permits, renewals, and biometric cards.
- **Extension filing deadline:** Applications for extension of a long-term residence permit for study must be submitted **no earlier than 120 days and no later than 1 day before** the expiration of the current permit.
- **Official booking portal:** Appointments for biometrics and document submission must be reserved through the official immigration portal https://frs.gov.cz/.
- **Required extension documents:**
  1. Green application form (*Žádost o povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu*).
  2. Valid travel passport (original).
  3. 1 passport photograph (if biometrics not already taken).
  4. Confirmation of study from VŠE (issued by your study department or printed with electronic stamp from InSIS).

5. Proof of accommodation (formular *Doklad o zajištění ubytování* or official dormitory confirmation).

title: Scholarships, campus building navigation and SafeQ printing at VŠE
text:

## Campus buildings and room code navigation
VŠE classrooms and offices are designated by building prefixes on the main Žižkov campus:
- **RB = Rajská budova (Paradise Building):** Houses the main entrance from nám. W. Churchilla, lecture halls (RB 101, RB 201), the Admission Office (RB 527), and International Office (OZS, 5th floor).
- **SB = Stará budova (Old Building):** Central wing featuring the historic Vencovského aula auditorium and lecture rooms.
- **NB = Nová budova (New Building):** Houses the main university library (Knihovna), computer study labs, student study departments (e.g. FIS on the 4th floor NB 403), and menza dining facilities.
- **JM = Jižní Město campus:** Satellite campus in Prague 4 (Kunratice) hosting specific freshman courses, sports grounds, and student dormitories.
- **Room decoding rule:** The first digit of a room code represents the floor. For example, `RB 209` is located in Rajská budova on the 2nd floor; `NB 403` is in Nová budova on the 4th floor.

# International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE

title: International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE
text:
International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE

## What is International Week (I-Week)?
- **Overview:** International Week (I-Week) is an intensive academic event organized by VŠE faculties (notably FIS, FPH, FIR) where visiting guest professors from top partner universities worldwide teach specialized courses in English.
- **Credits:** Each successfully completed International Week course awards **3 ECTS credits**.
- **Format and Schedule:** Unlike standard 13-week semester courses, I-Week courses are delivered in an intensive condensed block format over 3 to 4 days (e.g. Monday to Wednesday/Thursday with full-day interactive lectures, seminars, and a final group project or exam).
- **Attendance:** Due to the intensive format, 100% active attendance is mandatory across all scheduled sessions.
- **Target Audience:** Open to all degree students (Bachelor and Master across all VŠE faculties) as well as incoming international exchange/Erasmus students.

title: International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE
text:
International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE

## How to register for International Week courses
1. **Check Faculty Announcements:** Faculties publish the specific course codes, topics, syllabi, visiting lecturer profiles, and schedules several weeks prior to I-Week on their English websites (e.g., https://fis.vse.cz/english/ or https://fba.vse.cz/).
2. **Registration in InSIS:** Register via InSIS under **Student Portal → Registration/Enrollment of Courses** (or the extra-semestral course enrollment section).
3. **Capacity and Timing:** Capacity is strictly limited (typically 20–30 students per course) to allow interactive discussions. Places are filled quickly on a first-come, first-served basis once registration opens in InSIS.

title: International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE
text:
International Week intensive courses and elective courses in English at VŠE

## Elective courses in English at VŠE
In addition to I-Week, international and local students can register for regular semester-long elective courses in English across several categories:
- **Free University-Wide Electives (cV / oV):** Courses open to all VŠE students regardless of faculty. Students can enroll in subjects from business, data science, economics, culture, or management.
- **Faculty Electives (fV):** Specialized courses offered by your home faculty outside the core mandatory curriculum.
- **Minor Specialization Electives (sV):** Elective subjects tied to your chosen Master's Minor Specialization (*vedlejší specializace*).
- **Foreign Language Courses (sJ):** Language courses for credits (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Business English, and Czech for foreigners).
- **Sports Courses (TV):** Practical sports classes at the Třebešín and Jarov sports centers (1 ECTS).

## 6. Emergency numbers (Czech Republic)

Universal EU emergency line and Czech health/medical line – verified as
official numbers used throughout the Czech Republic:

- **112** – single European emergency number (police / fire / ambulance).
- **155** – Czech ambulance / medical rescue (záchranná služba).
- 158 – Police.
- 150 – Fire and rescue.
- 156 – Municipal / city police (Prague).
- Non-urgent medical help in Prague: 155 dispatcher will route you; English-
  speaking assistance is available on request.

(Source for numbers: general Czech emergency-number information; cross-check
on https://www.vse.cz/english/contacts/ or the Czech Ministry of Interior.)
